I've been working this land for thirty years. My father farmed before me. I don't read books about farming — I watch the crops, I watch the sky, I talk to the neighbors. Six mu is enough to feed my family and sell a little extra at market. I'll do what I always do, what works here in Quzhou.

**Wheat comes first.** I'll put all 6 mu into wheat after the autumn maize harvest, around late October. I'll plough with the rotary machine — I rent it from the village — to turn under the maize stalks. I use a good variety, the one the seed shop in town has been selling for years, the improved kind most people around here plant. For fertilizer, I'll put down compound fertilizer as base before seeding, then top-dress with urea when the wheat starts jointing in spring. I irrigate four times: before sowing, once in winter to protect the roots from cold, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice — once for aphids in spring, once for rust if I see it coming.

**Maize follows.** Right after I harvest the wheat in June, I seed the maize directly without ploughing — no time, the summer is short. I use hybrid seed, everyone does now, the yields are better. I apply fertilizer twice: some at planting, more when the stalks are knee-high. I irrigate when the soil looks dry or if rain doesn't come — maybe two or three times. One spray for corn borer if I see the leaves getting eaten.

This is the same as last year. Same as the year before. It feeds us.
